title: micro-mentorship-clinic-30-90-day-handoff
content:
Purpose:
A compact, practical playbook for running a 30→90 day micro-mentorship clinic geared at rapid onboarding and early contribution for newly hired ICs.

Scope / When to use:
- Use when hiring small batches (1–5) of engineers/designers/PMs where a short, focused mentor rotation accelerates impact.
- Designed for roles with a short ramp signal (product-facing, infra engineers, SRE).
- Not intended to replace role-level onboarding decks — it layers on top of role-specific 30/60/90s.

High-level goals:
1) Get new hire to own a tiny, customer-facing task within 30 days (bugfix, telemetry improvement, infra change).
2) Build a repeatable mentor rotation that captures tribal knowledge and reduces context-switch load on senior ICs.
3) Create a handoff artifact (living doc + 1 pager) that survives rotations.

Clinic schedule (30-day micro sprint):
- Day 0 (preboard): mentor assigned, calendar invites to 1:1s + weekly sync, access checklist validated (G-Suite, repo, jira).
- Day 1–3: rapid context drop — mentor walkthrough (60–90m), repo map, quick runbook, first PR template.
- Day 4–14: shadowing + small task assignment (pick one of the small task templates below). Mentor pairs twice a week.
- Day 15–21: independent ownership of small task; mentor available for unblock sessions only. Weekly demo to pod.
- Day 22–30: polish, docs, ship + create 1 pager: what I changed, why, rollforward/rollback, open questions.

Task templates (pick one):
- Telemetry gap: add end-to-end metric + dashboard tile for a critical flow.
- Minor reliability fix: fix flaky test or tighten alert threshold after triage.
- UXR cleanup: small UX tweak with A/B experiment flag.
- Infra housekeeping: add monitoring for a missing datastore metric, document runbook.

Mentor rotation model (roles & time commitments):
- Primary mentor (week 0–4): 2hrs/week direct pairing + asynchronous reviews (max 3hrs/week).
- Secondary mentor (domain SME): 1hr/week office hours, domain answer backlog.
- Buddy: peer-level 30–60m/week for social/ops questions.
- People Ops owner: 1h/week to track signals, remove blockers, and coordinate cross-team access.

Onboarding checklist (clinic-specific additions):
- Access: repo + CI + staging creds, ability to run tests locally documented.
- Observability: access to dashboards + able to view the metric worked on.
- Permissions: can open PRs and merge small changes after review policy.
- Communication: added to pod channel, given intro message template.
- Safety: routing plan for rollbacks and an assigned oncall contact.

Handoff artifact template (deliverable at day 30):
- One-page summary (goal, what shipped, how to validate, ownership going forward).
- PR links & incremental changelog.
- Runbook snippet (how to revert, who to call, expected side effects).
- Follow-ups/OKRs owner (next 60–90 day goal).

Interview / hiring signals used to choose clinic candidates:
- Preference for versatile ICs with evidence of quick domain pickup (past short ramp projects).
- Signal list: small-scope PRs, clear commit messages, prior mentorship experience, demonstrable autonomy.
- Negative signals: heavy legacy-system-only experience with no cross-functional examples (can still succeed but needs more time).

Interview rubric adjustments for clinic candidates (short form):
- Problem decomposition (15): looks for ability to scope a small deliverable and identify quick validation signals.
- Code craft / execution (25): focus on end-to-end small change (tests, CI, docs).
- Mentorship / collaboration (20): evidence they learn quickly and document work for others.
- Reliability mindset (20): logging, observability, rollback thinking.
- Communication (20): can explain plan in 5 minutes to non-expert.

Scoring thresholds (internal):
- Green (>=80): candidate is clinic-ready.
- Yellow (60–79): candidate needs extended 60-day handoff with heavier mentor bandwidth.
- Red (<60): not recommended for immediate hire into clinic; suggest standard 90d onboarding.

Signals to track (People Ops + hiring manager):
- Time to first merged PR.
- Number of unblock incidents escalated (target: 0–1 in first 30 days).
- Quality of doc handed off at day 30 (peer review score 1–5).
- Manager confidence after 30 days (quick pulse: red/yellow/green).

Risks & mitigations:
- Mentor burnout: cap mentor load to max 2 active mentees simultaneously.
- Access delays: people ops pre-validate 48h before start. Escalation path: people-ops > infra eng lead.
- Scope creep: tasks must fit a single sprint and have a clear rollback plan.

Notes to self / open questions (working doc style):
- Should we A/B two mentor models (daily pairing vs thrice-weekly office hours)? Try one cohort split in Q1.
- What is acceptable doc quality for the 1 pager? Draft rubric to avoid manager subjectivity.
- Link to onboarding deck that clinic should augment: confluence:HR/onboarding-deck-2025 (add pointer).

Operational checklist for People Ops (pre-run):
- Confirm mentor roster and backups.
- Prepare candidate selection slate.
- Reserve calendar blocks (pairing hours) for mentors.
- Create clinic cohort slack channel + inviteees.
- Prepare day-30 review rubric and schedule demo.

Example week 2 pairing script for mentor (copyable in slack):
- 0–10m: quick sync (how are you feeling, blockers).
- 10–40m: pair on the code path (share screen, explain commit plan).
- 40–50m: write tests together.
- 50–60m: next steps + assign 2 small follow-ups.

Appendix: micro-PR checklist (for quick review):
- Clear title + description (why, how to test, risk).
- Tests added or existing tests validated.
- Runbook/rollback section included.
- Observability: metric added or affected noted.
- Changelog entry or release note stub.

Quick retrospect template (post-cohort):
- What worked?
- What was the highest friction?
- Did new hires hit first-PR-in-30d target?
- Mentor feedback summary.
- Action items (owner + due date).

References & inspiration:
- confluence:HR/mentorship-experiments-2024
- Slack thread: #people-ops-mentorship (link pinned)
- JIRA:HR-4321 (pilot cohort backlog)

Version notes:
- v0.1 — initial draft (Asha P.) 2025-11-03
- v0.2 — added rubric + scoring 2025-12-10 (Liam C.)
- v0.3 — operational checklist + pilot adjustments 2026-01-12 (Riley M.)

---
Notes: informal items above are intentionally lightweight — this doc is a clinic runbook and will be iterated after each cohort.
